chapters.title: First sprouts
chapters.blurb: Print, variables, math, decisions and loops.

lessons.title: Say hello
goals: Use print() to show a message
Make the console say exactly: Hello, garden!
lessons.starter_code:
# Say hello to your garden
print("Hello, garden!")

rules.hint: Text goes inside quotes: print("Hello, garden!")

lessons.title: Name your water
goals: Create a variable named water and set it to 4
Print the variable
lessons.starter_code:
# Store a number in a variable, then print it
water = 4
print(water)

rules.hint: A variable is a name, an equals sign and a value: water = 4

lessons.title: Count the seeds
goals: Multiply seeds by pots using *
Print the total
lessons.starter_code:
seeds = 6
pots = 3
# Print how many seeds you need in total
print(seeds * pots)

rules.hint: You can put a calculation inside print: print(seeds * pots)

lessons.title: Sunny or not
goals: Write an if that checks sun > 5
Add an else for the other case
Print Grow! when the sun is bright

rules.hint: End the if line with a colon and indent the next line by 4 spaces.

lessons.title: Water every plant
goals: Use a for loop with range(3)
Print Water plant 1, Water plant 2 and Water plant 3
lessons.expected_output:
Water plant 1
Water plant 2
Water plant 3

rules.hint: range(3) counts 0, 1, 2. Print i + 1 to start at 1.

chapters.title: Sprouting Logic & Data
chapters.blurb: Lists, indexing, conditionals, and while loops.

lessons.title: Gather the Harvest
goals: Access the first element of harvest with [0]
Print the first vegetable
lessons.starter_code:
# Store 3 garden vegetables in a list
harvest = ["carrot", "tomato", "radish"]
# Print the first vegetable
print(harvest[0])

rules.hint: Lists in Python start at index 0: harvest[0]

lessons.title: Count the Petals
goals: Use len() to measure the flowers list
Print the length
lessons.starter_code:
flowers = ["rose", "tulip", "daisy", "sunflower"]
# Print how many flowers are in the garden
print(len(flowers))

rules.hint: len(flowers) returns the total number of items in the list.

lessons.title: Flower Bloom Checker
goals: Use an if condition with 'and'
Print Blooming! when both sun >= 7 and water >= 5
Add else block printing Wilting
lessons.starter_code:
sun = 10
water = 8
# If sun >= 7 and water >= 5, print Blooming! Otherwise print Wilting
if sun >= 7 and water >= 5:
    print("Blooming!")
else:
    print("Wilting")

rules.hint: Combine conditions with 'and': if sun >= 7 and water >= 5:

lessons.title: Watering While Sprouting
goals: Use a while loop checking drops > 0
Print 'Drop ' with current drops count
Subtract 1 from drops inside the loop
lessons.starter_code:
drops = 3
# Use a while loop to count down drops
while drops > 0:
    print("Drop " + str(drops))
    drops -= 1

rules.hint: Don't forget to decrease drops inside the while loop: drops -= 1

lessons.title: Garden Greeting Function
goals: Define a function named greet_plant with one parameter
Return greeting text
Call the function and print the result
lessons.starter_code:
# Define a function named greet_plant with one parameter
def greet_plant(name):
    return "Hello " + name

print(greet_plant("Daisy"))

rules.hint: Functions let you reuse code. Indent the function body with 4 spaces.

chapters.title: Master Garden Algorithms
chapters.blurb: Dictionaries, f-strings, list filtering, and algorithms.

lessons.title: Catalog the Seeds
goals: Access the sunflower price using prices['sunflower']
Print the price

rules.hint: Dictionary values are retrieved with their key: prices["sunflower"]

lessons.title: Greenhouse Temperature
goals: Use an f-string or formatting to combine variables
Print exactly: The Fern is at 24C
lessons.starter_code:
temp = 24
plant = "Fern"
# Print: The Fern is at 24C
print(f"The {plant} is at {temp}C")

rules.hint: Use formatted text: print(f"The {plant} is at {temp}C")

lessons.title: Weed Remover
goals: Loop over garden_bed
Use if item == 'flower':
Print only the flowers

rules.hint: Check each item inside the loop: if item == "flower": print(item)

lessons.title: Garden Grid Matrix
goals: Use nested for loops with range()
Print the plot coordinates for each cell
lessons.expected_output:
Plot (1,1)
Plot (1,2)
Plot (1,3)
Plot (2,1)
Plot (2,2)
Plot (2,3)

rules.hint: A loop inside another loop generates coordinates for rows and columns.

lessons.title: Ultimate Garden Simulator
goals: Sum all numbers in the crops list
Print exactly: Harvest total: 50
lessons.starter_code:
# Garden Simulator: Calculate total harvest seeds
crops = [10, 25, 15]
total = 0
for yield_amount in crops:
    total += yield_amount
print("Harvest total:", total)

rules.hint: Accumulate the sum with total += yield_amount inside your loop.
